note: imageapi_optimize_webp adds an ImageAPIOptimizeProcessor plugin id imageapi_optimize_webp (label 'WebP Deriver') that clones a styled image to .webp via imagewebp() at a configurable quality (default 75). You add it to an imageapi_optimize_pipeline (config entity, id key 'name', config prefix imageapi_optimize.pipeline.*, processors keyed by uuid with id/data/weight/uuid). Requires imageapi_optimize. No settings form/configure route/permissions/Drush. Introspection reads a pipeline's processor id and quality; execution builds a WebP pipeline and adds the processor to an empty pipeline. NOTE: on this shared site remote_stream_wrapper overrides ImageStyle without imageapi_optimize's hasPipeline(), so deleting a pipeline entity fatals during flush; the scripts therefore delete pipeline CONFIG via the config factory (\Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('imageapi_optimize.pipeline.X')->delete()) which is clean. No node operations.

evals.prompt: I use the ImageAPI Optimize (Image Optimize) module in Drupal and want to also generate WebP versions of my styled images. Which processor does the imageapi_optimize_webp module add that I should put in my pipeline, and what is its default image quality?
evals.expected_output: It adds the 'WebP Deriver' processor (plugin id imageapi_optimize_webp). Add it to an Image Optimize pipeline; its quality setting defaults to 75 (1-100). It clones each styled derivative to a .webp file.

evals.prompt: How do I actually turn on WebP output with imageapi_optimize_webp for my image styles?
evals.expected_output: Create an Image Optimize pipeline (Configuration > Media > Image Optimize pipelines), add the WebP Deriver processor to it, then assign that pipeline to individual image styles or set it as the site-wide default pipeline. The module generates and serves the .webp derivatives automatically.

evals.prompt: Once imageapi_optimize_webp has generated a .webp derivative, how does Drupal serve it, and what happens to the .webp when the image style is flushed?
evals.expected_output: It overrides the image.style_public / image.style_private route controller (ImageStyleDownloadController::deliver): a request for <derivative>.webp derives the source, generates the normal derivative, and returns the .webp with Content-Type image/webp when it exists. hook_image_style_flush deletes the matching .webp when the derivative is flushed.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is an Image Optimize pipeline named 'iow_intro'. Inspect it on the live site and state which processor plugin it runs.
evals.expected_output: The pipeline imageapi_optimize.pipeline.iow_intro contains one processor with id imageapi_optimize_webp (the WebP Deriver), configured at quality 60.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site an Image Optimize pipeline named 'iow_quality' uses the WebP Deriver processor. Inspect the live pipeline configuration and state the WebP image quality value it is set to.
evals.expected_output: The imageapi_optimize_webp processor in imageapi_optimize.pipeline.iow_quality has data.quality = 90.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create an Image Optimize pipeline named 'iow_task' that runs the imageapi_optimize_webp 'WebP Deriver' processor at image quality 80. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create an imageapi_optimize_pipeline config entity 'iow_task' (id key 'name') whose processors list contains an entry with id imageapi_optimize_webp and data.quality = 80, then save.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is an empty Image Optimize pipeline named 'iow_base' with no processors. Add the imageapi_optimize_webp 'WebP Deriver' processor to it and save the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add a processor entry with id imageapi_optimize_webp (uuid-keyed, with data.quality, weight) to the processors of imageapi_optimize.pipeline.iow_base and save the pipeline.
